title: 126. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Determining Units of Derived Quantities
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Unit of Speed from Its Defining Equation
questions.learningObjective: Determine the derived SI unit of speed in base units.
questions.question: What is the derived SI unit of speed expressed in base SI units?
questions.explanation: Speed is defined by \(v=\frac{d}{t}\), where \(d\) is distance in metres and \(t\) is time in seconds. Therefore, the unit of speed is \(\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}\). Option B is not correct because multiplying metres by seconds does not match the definition of speed.
questions.hint: Start from a defining equation for the requested physical quantity.

questions.concept: Unit of Acceleration from Velocity Change
questions.learningObjective: Determine the derived SI unit of acceleration in base units.
questions.question: What is the derived SI unit of acceleration expressed in base SI units?
questions.explanation: Acceleration is defined by \(a=\frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}\). The change in velocity has unit \(\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}\), and the time interval has unit \(\text{s}\). Therefore, the unit of acceleration is \(\frac{\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}}{\text{s}}=\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}^2}\). Option B has the wrong power relationship.
questions.hint: Express the quantities in mass, length, and time units.

questions.concept: Unit of Force from Newton's Second Law
questions.learningObjective: Determine the derived SI unit of force in base units.
questions.question: What is the derived SI unit of force expressed in base SI units?
questions.explanation: Force is defined by \(F=ma\). Mass has unit \(\text{kg}\), and acceleration has unit \(\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}^2}\). Therefore, the unit of force is \(\text{kg}\cdot\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}^2}\), which is the newton. Option A is the unit of energy, not force.
questions.hint: Combine the exponents of the base SI units.

questions.concept: Unit of Work from Force and Displacement
questions.learningObjective: Determine the derived SI unit of work in base units.
questions.question: What is the derived SI unit of work expressed in base SI units?
questions.explanation: Work is defined by \(W=Fd\). The unit of force is \(\text{kg}\cdot\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}^2}\), and the unit of displacement is \(\text{m}\). Multiplying gives \(\frac{\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2}{\text{s}^2}\), which is the joule. Option B is the unit of force.
questions.hint: Start from a defining equation for the requested physical quantity.

questions.concept: Unit of Power from Work and Time
questions.learningObjective: Determine the derived SI unit of power in base units.
questions.question: What is the derived SI unit of power expressed in base SI units?
questions.explanation: Power is defined by \(P=\frac{W}{t}\). The unit of work is \(\frac{\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2}{\text{s}^2}\), and the unit of time is \(\text{s}\). Dividing gives \(\frac{\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2}{\text{s}^3}\), which is the watt. Option B is the unit of work or energy.
questions.hint: Express the quantities in mass, length, and time units.

questions.concept: Unit of Pressure from Force and Area
questions.learningObjective: Determine the derived SI unit of pressure in base units.
questions.question: What is the derived SI unit of pressure expressed in base SI units?
questions.explanation: Pressure is defined by \(P=\frac{F}{A}\). The unit of force is \(\text{kg}\cdot\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}^2}\), and the unit of area is \(\text{m}^2\). Dividing gives \(\frac{\text{kg}\cdot\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}^2}}{\text{m}^2}=\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{m}\cdot\text{s}^2}\). Option A is the unit of energy.
questions.hint: Combine the exponents of the base SI units.

questions.concept: Unit of Density from Mass and Volume
questions.learningObjective: Determine the derived SI unit of density in base units.
questions.question: What is the derived SI unit of density expressed in base SI units?
questions.explanation: Density is defined by \(\rho=\frac{m}{V}\). The unit of mass is \(\text{kg}\), and the unit of volume is \(\text{m}^3\). Therefore, the unit of density is \(\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{m}^3}\). Option A incorrectly multiplies mass by volume.
questions.hint: Start from a defining equation for the requested physical quantity.

questions.concept: Unit of Momentum from Mass and Velocity
questions.learningObjective: Determine the derived SI unit of momentum in base units.
questions.question: What is the derived SI unit of momentum expressed in base SI units?
questions.explanation: Momentum is defined by \(p=mv\). The unit of mass is \(\text{kg}\), and the unit of velocity is \(\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}\). Multiplying gives \(\text{kg}\cdot\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}\). Option A is the unit of force.
questions.hint: Express the quantities in mass, length, and time units.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the derived SI unit of frequency in base units.
questions.question: What is the derived SI unit of frequency expressed in base SI units?
questions.explanation: Frequency is defined by \(f=\frac{1}{T}\), where \(T\) is the period in seconds. Therefore, the unit of frequency is \(\frac{1}{\text{s}}\), also called the hertz. Option A is the unit of time or period, not frequency.
questions.hint: Combine the exponents of the base SI units.

questions.concept: Unit of Spring Constant from Hooke's Law
questions.learningObjective: Determine the derived SI unit of the spring constant in base units.
questions.question: Hooke's law is \(F=kx\). What is the derived SI unit of the spring constant \(k\) expressed in base SI units?
questions.explanation: From \(F=kx\), we have \(k=\frac{F}{x}\). The unit of force is \(\text{kg}\cdot\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}^2}\), and the unit of displacement \(x\) is \(\text{m}\). Dividing gives \(\frac{\text{kg}\cdot\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}^2}}{\text{m}}=\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{s}^2}\). Option A is the unit of force, not the spring constant.
questions.hint: Start from a defining equation for the requested physical quantity.
